title: Endeavour Systems assurance intake & controls mapping
summary: Initial SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture intake for Endeavour Systems. Covered scope boundaries, Trust Center access, control ownership mapping, KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention and fields, RBAC/SSO integration (SAML + SCIM), and next steps to share reports and schedule deep dive for VPC onboarding.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share latest SOC 2 Type II report and Trust Center link by 2026-08-10
Ravi Patel: Produce KMS integration diagram (BYOK and Redwood-managed) and sample KMS policy by 2026-08-12
Priya Nair: Provide list of regulatory regions (EU, CA) and data residency constraints by 2026-08-11
next_steps: Redwood to grant Endeavour read-only Trust Center access (scoped to Compliance team)
Schedule 90-min technical deep dive for VPC/private deployment with Hannah and infra team week of 2026-08-17
Deliver control mapping spreadsheet (Redwood controls vs Endeavour control IDs)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Tom Blake (Endeavour CISO), Priya Nair (Endeavour Head Cloud Eng), José Ramirez (Endeavour Compliance Manager), Hannah Lee (Endeavour DevOps)
Shared artifacts mentioned: Trust Center link (https://trust.redwood.ai/endeavour-readonly), SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (sent), KMS_flow_sketch_v2.pptx

00:00 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have the core team on. quick agenda — purely intake, we want to understand scope for SOC 2 / ISO mapping, trust center access, a few technical items: KMS, logs, RBAC, SSO. anything to add from your side?
00:18 Tom Blake (Endeavour CISO): No that covers it. Main ask up front — we need to know which controls you cover vs what we need to own, and whether we can get your latest Type II report and the evidence bundle or at least read-only access to the Trust Center. We're doing our gap analysis for September audit.
00:35 Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll share the Type II report, the carve-out/coverage matrix, and we can set you up with read-only Trust Center access scoped to your compliance group. Ravi, quick note on the logs and KMS?
00:48 Ravi Patel (Redwood SE): Yeah, two things to call out — audit logs are tenant-scoped, and we store event logs for control plane actions and runtime invocation metadata. we need to clarify what fields you need — e.g., user id, request id, model id, and whether you require full prompt content in logs or redacted traces. also KMS — we support both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK via customer KMS, we have HSM-backed options depending on plan.
01:12 Priya Nair (Endeavour Head Cloud Eng): For regulatory reasons EU data residency is must for some workloads. We need to confirm where data sits and whether keys can be region-bound. Also we want to know if the KV cache contains unencrypted user content server-side.
01:29 Ravi: Good question. The KV cache is encrypted at rest; by default the encryption keys are Redwood-managed, but with BYOK you can bring a regional key so cached state in that region is encrypted under your key. small caveat — cross-region fallback can use a compatible model variant, we can scope that out in the VPC config.
01:50 José Ramirez (Endeavour Compliance Manager): On audit logs — retention and tamper-evidence are our big asks. Are logs append-only? Can you provide digest/hash-chain or attestations for the period necessary for our ISO audits?
02:05 Ravi: We maintain write-once append behavior for event streams in the trust center. We export tamper-evidence via signed digests for audit periods on request — that's part of our enterprise package. for hosted customers we can provide signed snapshots for the same retention windows.
02:28 Hannah Lee (DevOps): If we go Private (VPC) what is in scope vs hosted? like, do we still need Redwood to produce certain evidence or is it all on us?
02:40 Maya: Good — we usually map responsibilities in a shared control matrix. Redwood covers the service-side controls: model serving, runtime, kernel selection, key management endpoints, and trace logging. Customer covers network controls inside the VPC, host hardening, and identity provider configuration. We'll send a control-mapping spreadsheet that makes this explicit.
03:05 Tom: Perfect. Can you run through RBAC options? Our auditors want least privilege and an auditor role that can only read logs and reports, not trigger deployments.
03:18 Ravi: We have three adjustable org roles out of the box: Org Admin, DevOps (deploy), and Auditor (read-only). SSO via SAML is supported with SCIM provisioning for groups so you can map your IdP groups to roles. MFA enforced via IdP. there are also per-route tokens for service integrations.
03:40 Priya: Does the Auditor role see prompt contents or only metadata?
03:45 Ravi: Auditor sees metadata and full logs only if you enable content retention. By default we redact prompt content in the Trust Center view unless you opt in for full-record retention; we label that in the UI. For compliance we can configure a keystroke where logs include full prompts but encrypted under your BYOK so Redwood can't read them.
04:05 José: That BYOK + encrypted logs model — does Redwood have access to the unencrypted plaintext for debugging?
04:12 Ravi: No, not if you use BYOK with key policies that disallow Redwood key usage. we do provide an emergency process (with legal/contract gate) if you need debug support — that would require explicit key escrow procedures we can document.
04:30 Maya: We'll include the BYOK flow and required IAM/KMS policy snippets in the KMS diagram.
04:38 Hannah: Regarding audit trails for model rollouts — we need traceability of which model version served which request for a date range. Are model hashes part of the logs?
04:50 Ravi: Yes, model sha/hash and version tag are included in the invocation logs. we also capture rollout change events in the control plane audit log with user id and timestamp.
05:05 Tom: Great. On evidence delivery — can you push artifacts to our SFTP or integrate with our internal evidence collection tooling?
05:13 Maya: We can provide S3 export, SFTP, or direct API pulls from Trust Center. for large evidence bundles we usually put a signed snapshot into a customer-specific S3 bucket or share a time-limited download.
05:28 Priya: A question on network logs — do you keep connection-level logs like source IP, TLS handshake metadata, and region endpoint? that's relevant for us to show network-flow controls.
05:40 Ravi: We record connection metadata at the edge: source IP (redacted per privacy), region, TLS version, and certificate fingerprint. We can enable IP retention for whitelist auditors if necessary but default scrub is to hash IPs for privacy.
06:00 José: For ISO mapping — A.8 and A.10, we need to map sub-controls. can Redwood provide a mapping to ISO 27001 annex A against your control IDs?
06:12 Maya: Yes. We'll provide a control mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 CC and ISO A.* entries, and mark which are in-scope for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
06:25 Tom: Can you also call out residual risks we should be aware of, like prompt leakage via logs or third-party plugin calls?
06:33 Ravi: We'll put a residual risk section. On plugins we don't currently allow arbitrary third-party plugins in hosted by default; any tool-calls are explicit and logged. Prompts in logs are the main surface — recommended mitigation is BYOK + restricted retention or runtime redaction heuristics.
06:58 Hannah: For our engineering team: what's the onboarding flow and how long does it take for VPC private deployment? we have a two-week window ideally.
07:08 Maya: For a standard VPC private deployment we typically do a 4–6 week onboarding including infra provisioning, VPN, KMS setup, and runbook handover. If you want a two-week fast path we can do an accelerated pilot for a single environment but scaled production generally needs more time.
07:28 Priya: Are you able to sign a data processing addendum and specific region residency clauses?
07:35 Maya: Yes, DPA plus region residency clauses are standard enterprise add-ons. legal can propose language in the MSA.
07:42 José: Audit log retention window — we're looking at 7 years for certain financial controls. Can Redwood retain logs that long?
07:50 Ravi: We can support extended retention for enterprise agreements — logs can be archived off to cold storage (S3 Glacier-like) and we can provide signed manifests for each archive. We'll note the cost impact in the proposal.
08:05 Tom: One more, evidence for patch management and change control on the runtime — do you provide CVE disclosure and patch dates?
08:15 Ravi: Yes, we publish a runtime CVE timeline in the Trust Center with patch dates and we can export a per-month change log for audits.
08:25 Priya: For the SCIM config — are group syncs one-way or two-way? we need to disable user-managed updates from Redwood side.
08:35 Ravi: SCIM is one-way provisioning from your IdP to Redwood. we don't allow Redwood-side user edits when SCIM is enabled. group-to-role mapping is configurable by the Org Admin.
08:50 Tom: Ok sounds like we have the key pieces. let's surface the next steps so we can close our gap analysis.
08:56 Maya: Quick recap then: Redwood will share Type II report and Trust Center access, KMS diagram, and control-mapping spreadsheet. Endeavour will share region constraints and any specific auditor accounts to provision. we'll schedule the private deployment deep dive next week.
09:12 José: Fine. Also, one small ask — can you provide a redacted sample evidence pack so our internal auditors see the format?
09:20 Maya: Yes, we can prepare a redacted example. We'll attach that with the SOC report.
09:28 Hannah: On practicalities — do you log the exact prompt that produced PII? we need to know retention policies for PII in prompts.
09:36 Ravi: By default prompt PII is redacted from the Trust Center UI; if you enable full retention it's encrypted under your key. We also provide automated redaction hooks you can run prior to sending to the API.
09:50 Tom: Competitors — just to be transparent, we've been evaluating BigCloudAI for the BYOK story and InferServe for the private deployment speed. Your differentiators here are the Trust Center and signed digests, which look good.
10:05 Maya: Noted. We'll emphasize the signed digest offering and the region-bound BYOK flow in the documents.
10:12 Priya: For the control mapping spreadsheet — can we get an initial draft in 5 business days? that aligns with our audit prep.
10:20 Maya: We'll target 2026-08-12 for the control mapping sheet.
10:25 José: Okay. Any blocker from Redwood side for scheduling the deep dive?
10:30 Maya: No, we'll propose times for week of 2026-08-17 after we share the materials.
10:40 Tom: Great. thanks everyone.

[End of meeting]
